note: SSH lands in WSL2 bash on GPU-BOX; all Windows facts below came from powershell.exe, not WSL.

cpu.name: AMD EPYC 7402P 24-Core Processor
cpu.isa_note: Zen 2 - AVX2 only; no AVX-512. Plan requires host code compiled without AVX-512.

reconciliation.reported_128_gb_claim: NOT confirmed. Six 16 GiB DIMMs populate 6 of 8 channels.
reconciliation.conclusion: The box currently has 6 DIMMs / 95.87 GiB usable. The 128 GB figure in the plan is the board's 8-slot capacity, not installed memory. Any earlier 112 GB reading is not reproduced.

pattern.occurrences: exactly one per boot, ~23 s after boot
pattern.runtime_recurrence: none observed in 37.6 h of continuous uptime

whea.revised_interpretation: This is a BOOT-TIME memory-path fault, not a runtime one. It fires once per boot ~23 s in, then does not recur for the life of the uptime (37.6 h clean at time of check). The practical consequence is a permanently reduced DIMM population (6 of 8 slots usable), not an expectation that a long GPU workload will crash the box.
whea.check_101_consequence: UPDATED: heavy testing is NOT gated by runtime instability on this evidence. What CHECK-101 still lacks is a resolved root cause and a repaired DIMM/CPU path. Treat the machine as stable-but-degraded: 95.87 GiB usable is the budget, and any future RAM change invalidates A/B comparisons across it. The earlier 'pause heavy testing' reading in commit ecaad19 overstated the risk; this supersedes it.
whea.root_cause_status: unresolved; prior lab note attributes it to the CPU socket. Unverified here.

storage.note: A 257 GB model download does not fit on C:. D: has 639 GB free and E: has 298 GB free.

gpu.adapter_ram_note: WMI AdapterRAM is a 32-bit field and caps at ~4 GiB; real per-card capacity is 32 GB. Do not use this value as a budget.
gpu.display_adapter_separate: Microsoft Basic Display Adapter (ASPEED, VEN_1A03&DEV_2000) - desktop is on the BMC, not a B70. Good: no B70 loses VRAM to dwm.
gpu.pcie_link_telemetry: UNKNOWN - not captured. Windows does not expose negotiated link generation/width for these adapters via the CIM classes available here; requires vendor tooling or dxdiag.

pnp_device_status.note: Get-PnpDevice reports Status=Unknown for several B70 entries. That is a PnP state-reporting quirk for these adapters, not a fault: all four enumerate in sycl-ls and all four were exercised successfully in session 3 GPU runs.
pnp_device_status.separate_amd_igpu: PCI\VEN_1002&DEV_13C0 (AMD Radeon integrated) present but unused for this work

missing_access.windows_fork_base_1c360526_full_commit: still unresolved - requires git fetch origin in the strata tree

second_pass_note: Second read-only pass closed the runtime-identity gaps listed in the original missing_access block. Method: sycl-ls run both WITHOUT and WITH the oneAPI setvars environment. The no-env run exposes only OpenCL devices; Level Zero devices appear only with setvars applied. Capturing only the no-env run would have under-reported the GPU backends actually in use.

oneapi_compiler.dpcpp_note: dpcpp is deprecated by Intel; wrapper prints 'use icx -fsycl'. Both resolve to the 2026.0 compiler.

unified_runtime.note: Two UR loader versions on disk; setvars selects the toolkit on PATH (2026.0).
unified_runtime.pi_level_zero_dll: not found as a standalone file (absorbed into the UR/L0 adapter layout)

sycl_devices.method: sycl-ls with oneAPI setvars applied (Level Zero visible); repeat without setvars shows OpenCL only
sycl_devices.env_note: ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR and SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER are both EMPTY after setvars. This matters: setting either one is what silently killed llama_context construction in this session's earlier work.
